comment: Level-of-detail knobs for the 3D client. Two independent channels: 'entity' is the coarse per-entity render channel, 'detail' is the screen-coverage detail ladder that picks how much geometry, animation and effect volume each entity gets. Nothing here is simulated — every value is client presentation only, so changing it can never desync a lockstep match. The manual LOD control in the client bar (auto/high/medium/low/off) overrides the measured level: 'high' pins the close rung on everything (instanced pools must be sized for that), 'off' shows strategic glyphs only.

entity.comment: Master switch for the per-entity LOD channel. false = every entity renders at its authored close-tier presentation regardless of screen size; useful when bisecting a visual bug that might be an LOD transition.

detail.comment: AUTO measures projected screen coverage to choose the same presentations used by the manual controls: close/HIGH, mid/MED, far/LOW, or glyph/removal/OFF. The first three are authored geometry rungs; OFF is the end state, showing strategic entity glyphs while removing vegetation and effect geometry. One deadband (thresholds.hysteresisPx) covers every AUTO transition. rebuildBudgetPerFrame caps how many entity meshes may rebuild per frame during camera sweeps; entities over budget keep their previous rung until a later frame. Entity glyphs fade in on top of the still-opaque LOW model, then replace that model after the glyph threshold.
detail.whichWayToTurnTheKnobs: EVERY threshold here is an apparent SIZE, and apparent size falls off as 1/distance -- so the sign is inverted from what "push it further away" suggests. RAISE a threshold and the transition moves CLOSER to the camera (it happens sooner as you zoom out); LOWER it and the transition is PUSHED OUT (detail survives farther away). The distance a boundary actually lands at is d = radiusWorld * (referenceViewportHeightPx/2) / tan(fovY/2) / T_px, i.e. radiusWorld * 1303.7 / T_px at the default 45 degree FOV. With today's values that puts the OFF flip (lowToOffPx=5) at 7822wu for a 30wu-collision-radius entity, LOW->MED (10) at 3911wu and MED->HIGH (15) at 2607wu; double the entity radius and every one of those distances doubles. To shift the WHOLE ladder in or out without changing its shape, move referenceViewportHeightPx instead (raising it pushes every boundary out).
detail.howItWorks: Every entity's projected screen radius, screenPx = radiusWorld * (referenceViewportHeightPx/2) / tan(fovY/2) / distance, is compared against thresholds.* to pick its level. (Internally the renderer normalises that radius into a 0..1 coverage level L before comparing, but the comparison is equivalent and nothing is authored in L.) Because the pixel math uses a FIXED reference viewport height rather than the real one, the same camera picks the same rungs on a 4K monitor as on a laptop, and window resizes or DPR changes never re-tier the world. The result is latched into one of four discrete levels -- OFF/glyph(0), LOW/far(1), MED/mid(2), HIGH/close(3); the code still spells them glyph/far/mid/close -- and only that discrete level is consumed downstream, so an entire zoom sweep costs at most three mesh rebuilds per entity instead of a continuous stream of them. Big units and buildings hold detail longer than small ones for free, because they occupy more pixels at the same distance.
detail.referenceViewportHeightPxComment: The virtual viewport height, in px, that all screen-radius math is measured against. Not the real canvas height -- pinning it makes LOD resolution- and DPR-independent, and makes recorded threshold numbers comparable across machines. RAISE = everything measures larger, so EVERY boundary pushes further out together; LOWER = the whole ladder pulls in toward the camera. This is the one knob that shifts the ladder without changing its shape -- a global sensitivity dial, not a quality setting.

thresholds.comment: The three LOD boundaries, named for the bar controls they switch between (HIGH/MED/LOW/OFF) and all expressed in the SAME unit: projected screen radius in px, measured at referenceViewportHeightPx. An entity is HIGH above highToMedPx, MED down to medToLowPx, LOW down to lowToOffPx, and OFF (strategic glyph, no geometry) below that. The radius being projected is the entity's COLLISION volume -- the same size the glyph itself is drawn at -- never a visual mesh estimate. LOW is deliberately the widest band: it is real geometry and should hold until the entity is genuinely too small on screen to be worth rendering, which is what lowToOffPx (a 5px radius, a 10px-wide blob) is asking. Direction: every one of these is an apparent SIZE and size falls off as 1/distance, so RAISING a threshold pulls that transition CLOSER to the camera and LOWERING it PUSHES it further out. Distance the boundary lands at: d = radiusWorld * (referenceViewportHeightPx/2) / tan(fovY/2) / threshold, i.e. radiusWorld * 1303.7 / threshold at the default 45 degree FOV -- so for an entity whose COLLISION radius is 30wu the OFF flip is at 7822wu, LOW at 3911wu and MED at 2607wu, and an entity of twice that radius holds each one twice as far out. To shift the whole ladder in or out without changing its shape, move referenceViewportHeightPx instead. The renderer normalises these into an internal 0..1 coverage level L, but nothing is authored in L any more -- px is the only unit you tune. highToMedPx and lowToOffPx are also the two ends of the strategic-glyph cross-fade: the glyph starts fading in the moment an entity drops off HIGH and is fully opaque by the OFF flip, drawn BEHIND the still-opaque model (far shell of the entity sphere) so it reads as a backdrop rather than an overlay.
thresholds.hysteresisPxComment: Deadband on every boundary, in the same px unit: a boundary must be overshot by this much before the entity actually changes level, in either direction. This is what stops an entity parked on a threshold from rebuilding its mesh every frame. Too small = visible thrash and rebuild-budget starvation during slow zooms; too large = visibly stale detail after a camera move. The OFF flip is exempt -- it is never blocked by the deadband.

rebuildBudgetPerFrame.comment: Cap on how many entities may rebuild their meshes in a single frame because their rung changed. Rung changes are a band-only rebuild; entities over budget simply keep last frame's presentation and are picked up on a later frame, so the cost of a fast zoom is spread out instead of spiking. Core-key changes (owner, blueprint, graphics settings) bypass this and always rebuild.

radiusFloor.comment: Minimum world radius, in world units, used for the coverage math on things whose visible footprint is much larger than their physical body. RAISE = that class measures bigger, so its transitions push further out; LOWER = they pull in toward the camera. -- a projectile's trail or a beam's glow reads on screen long after the body itself is sub-pixel. Without a floor these would flip to glyph/removal while still clearly visible. Purely a measurement fudge: it inflates the input radius, it does not change the thresholds.

featureMinRung.comment: Lowest LOD level at which each named feature is still built, in the same HIGH/MED/LOW/OFF vocabulary as the thresholds above: low=1, medium=2, high=3 ('off' is the glyph end state and builds nothing). A 'low' feature survives all the way to the OFF flip; a 'high' feature sheds first when zooming out. Direction: moving a feature high -> medium -> low pushes its disappearance further from the camera; medium -> high brings it in. The legacy far/mid/close spellings are still accepted and mean low/medium/high.
featureMinRung.whatEachFeatureIs: body = the chassis/hull mesh itself. healthBar / nameLabel = the HUD sprites over the entity (these also fade separately by camera distance via entityHudConfig). turret = the turret mount assembly; turretHead = its rotating head; barrelPrimary / barrelSecondary = the main and secondary barrel geometry. muzzleDetail = muzzle brakes/flash hardware on the barrel tip. locomotion = wheels/legs/treads/hover rig geometry; locomotionAnimated = whether that rig is rigged for movement at all (below it the rig is static geometry); treadCleats = the individual tread cleat/end-cap detail. chassisDetail = secondary hull greebles. buildingDetail = the building's non-silhouette detail pass. shieldPanels = shield dome panel geometry. projectileTrail / projectileGlow = shot trail ribbon and its additive glow. beamGlow = the beam's inner glow layers (the beam core is always drawn).

building.comment: Per-archetype visual gates for the hand-authored building meshes, same low/medium/high ladder as featureMinRung. typeDetails = the parts that say what KIND of building this is (extractor head, solar dish, radar rig) and so must survive far out; largeAnimation = its big moving/glowing parts; tinyTrim = pipework, vents, bolts and other sub-pixel greebles, kept at high only.

tower.comment: Same ladder for defensive towers. launcherDetails = the launcher/emitter hardware that identifies the tower at a glance; animationAndGlow = spin rigs and emissive glow; smallTrim = fine surface trim, high only.

animation.comment: Live per-frame animation shedding (no mesh rebuild). Below unitAnimationMinRung, barrel spin freezes and locomotion rigs (tread scroll, wheel spin, leg gait, floor clamps) update every locomotionFarFrameStride frames with accumulated dt instead of every frame. Building animators (wind/extractor/radar/solar) freeze below buildingAnimationMinRung.
animation.whyItIsSeparate: These gates cost nothing to cross -- geometry is untouched, only the per-frame update work is skipped -- so they can sit at a higher rung than the geometry gates above. Frozen state is RETAINED, not reset: a gatling that freezes mid-spin resumes from the same angle, and strided locomotion accumulates dt so EMAs stay frame-rate independent (it just goes stride-stale, never wrong). The freeze must stay level-triggered rather than edge-triggered, or a re-sync silently re-arms the animator every frame.
animation.locomotionFarFrameStrideComment: Once gated, run the locomotion rig every Nth frame instead of every frame. 1 = no throttle. Large values are cheap but make wheels/treads visibly step.

effectSpawnScale.comment: Per-authored-rung spawn scales. AUTO resolves to exactly one of these three values; glyph/removal spawns no effect geometry.
effectSpawnScale.whatItScales: A multiplier on how many particles/quads an effect emits, applied at spawn time by the rung of the emitting entity. It thins the effect rather than shrinking it, so a distant explosion still reads at the right size and duration, just with fewer pieces. Values are clamped to [0,1]; close is normally 1 (author the effect for close range, then thin it out).
